statement: On a compact doubling domain with a uniformly Lipschitz score class, bounded conditionally unbiased targets and squared-loss ERM imply a high-probability uniform approximation error equal to approximation error plus O(L_H^(d/(d+2)) (log(n/delta)/n)^(1/(d+2))).

quantifiers.sample_size: the asserted asymptotic rate must hold for all sufficiently large n
quantifiers.estimator: an empirical squared-loss minimizer, or a method satisfying Lemma 4
quantifiers.constant: a finite big-O constant independent of n

assumptions: The relevant domain is compact and has finite doubling dimension.
Every hypothesis is uniformly Lipschitz and maps into [0,1].
Bounded conditionally unbiased targets are available for every domain point.
The chosen estimator is a valid empirical squared-loss minimizer.
falsification_condition: A deterministic family satisfies every displayed assumption for every n, has zero approximation error, but a valid ERM has sup-norm error one while the claimed rate tends to zero.
